name: Thracian Tomb of Sveshtari
description: This 3rd-century BC Getic tomb lies in a burial mound near the village of Sveshtari in northeast Bulgaria, found in 1982. Inside the central chamber, ten women carved in high relief, half human and half plant, rise from the walls as painted caryatids, with more painted scenes above in the vault. Nothing like them has turned up elsewhere in Thrace, and the tomb may have belonged to the Getic king Dromichaetes.
